name: LMR51430XDDCR
title: Synchronous 3 A step-down converter, 4.5 V to 36 V input, SOT-23
summary: A step-down converter with both power MOSFETs on chip, taking 4.5 V to 36 V in and delivering up to 3 A at an output set by two resistors from 0.6 V up to 95 % of the input. It uses fixed-frequency peak-current-mode control with internal compensation and a fixed 4 ms soft start. Four versions differ in switching frequency (500 kHz or 1.1 MHz) and in light-load behaviour: PFM versions skip pulses for efficiency, FPWM versions keep switching at constant frequency. Protection covers cycle-by-cycle peak and valley current limits, hiccup on a sustained short, input UVLO, a precision enable and thermal shutdown.
key_figures: 0.12 Ω high side, 0.07 Ω low side, typ at 25 °C

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Power ground; inside, it is the low-side FET source. Goes to system ground and to the ground ends of CIN and COUT, with the shortest possible path to CIN.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node, where the high-side FET source meets the low-side FET drain. It drives the power inductor.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply for the internal bias LDO and the high-side FET. Takes the input supply and the input bypass capacitors CIN, which sit directly across VIN and GND.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input; a resistor divider from the output sets VOUT. Must never be shorted to ground while the converter runs.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Precision enable: high turns the converter on, low turns it off, and an open pin leaves the device disabled, so it must not float. May be tied to VIN; an external resistor divider on it sets an adjustable UVLO.

pins.name: CB
pins.function: Bootstrap supply for the high-side gate driver: a good-quality 100 nF capacitor goes from CB to SW.

notes: Top view: pins 1 to 3 (GND, SW, VIN) run down the left side, pins 4 to 6 (FB, EN, CB) up the right, CB opposite GND.
Pin types: A analog, P power, G ground.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: The bare minimum around the converter: an input capacitor across VIN and GND, EN strapped to VIN so the part starts whenever the supply is up, a bootstrap capacitor between CB and SW, an inductor and output capacitor filtering SW into VOUT, and a two-resistor divider from VOUT to FB. The input may be up to 36 V.

circuits.title: Application circuit, 12 V to 5 V
circuits.description: A 12 V input converted to 5 V at up to 3 A at 500 kHz. CIN, 2.2 µF, decouples the input; EN is tied to VIN; CBOOT, 0.1 µF, feeds the high-side driver from SW; a 6.8 µH inductor and 44 µF of output capacitance filter the switch node; RFBT 100 kΩ over RFBB 13.7 kΩ give 5 V from the 0.6 V reference.
notes: In the worked design for this circuit the input capacitance is two 4.7 µF, 50 V X7R parts with a 0.1 µF high-frequency capacitor close to the pins, the output capacitance is two 22 µF, 25 V X7R ceramics of about 5 mΩ ESR, and the inductor is a 6.8 µH ferrite part rated 4 A RMS and 5 A saturation.

operation.text: A synchronous buck from 4.5 V to 36 V delivering up to 3 A, regulated by fixed-frequency peak-current-mode control with its loop compensated internally, so few outside parts are needed. PFM versions drop into pulse-frequency mode at light load for efficiency; FPWM versions keep a constant switching frequency for low ripple and tight regulation. Built in: precision enable, internal soft start, thermal shutdown, input UVLO, cycle-by-cycle current limit and hiccup short-circuit protection.

While the high-side NMOS conducts, SW sits near VIN and the inductor current climbs at (VIN - VOUT) / L; once it switches off, the low-side NMOS takes over after a dead time and the current falls at -VOUT / L. The voltage loop sets a peak-current command from the output error; the current through the high-side switch is measured, and the switch opens once it reaches that command. Switching frequency stays fixed under normal load.

The output is set by a divider from VOUT to FB against the 0.6 V reference. 1 % resistors with low temperature coefficient are recommended; divider tolerance and drift enter the output accuracy. RFBT between 10 kΩ and 100 kΩ is recommended. A smaller RFBT pre-loads the output and reduces the offset in PFM, at a cost in very-light-load efficiency; a larger one draws less current but makes FB more open to noise, and more than 1 MΩ is not recommended.

EN below 0.95 V shuts the device down; above 1.36 V the converter starts. EN must not be left open. Tying EN to VIN starts the converter whenever VIN is in range. A divider RENT over RENB from VIN sets a precise system UVLO, usable for sequencing or for a battery discharge cut-off, and a logic signal may also drive EN. EN must not exceed VIN + 0.3 V, and no voltage should be put on EN while VIN is 0 V.

operation.topic: Minimum on time, minimum off time and frequency foldback
operation.text: The high-side switch has a 70 ns minimum on time and a 150 ns minimum off time, which bound the conversion ratio at full frequency. Once either limit is reached the switching frequency folds back: at high input the on time stays at its minimum and the frequency drops so the duty cycle can fall further; at low input the off time stays at its minimum and the frequency drops, to roughly 133 kHz, so the duty cycle can rise. This keeps the output in regulation over a wider input range and lowers the effective dropout.
A capacitor between CB and SW powers the high-side gate drive and is recharged while the low-side switch is on. 0.1 µF is recommended, ceramic X7R or X5R, rated 16 V or more.

Both a peak and a valley inductor current limit apply. The high-side current, sensed after a blanking time, is limited every cycle by the clamped peak threshold. The low-side current is also sensed: if it is still above the valley limit at the end of a cycle, the low-side switch stays on until the current falls below it, and only then does the high-side switch turn on again. If FB is below 40 % of VREF and the valley limit is hit for 256 consecutive cycles, the converter enters hiccup: it shuts off for tHICCUP, 135 ms typ, then restarts, repeating until the fault clears. In FPWM versions the inductor current may reverse; if it passes the negative limit the low-side switch turns off and the high-side switch turns on at once.

The internal reference ramps up over 4.0 ms typ at enable or power-up to limit inrush. During start-up an overcurrent blanking time, tOCP_BLK of 33 ms typ, keeps the current limit from tripping hiccup while a large output capacitance charges at high VOUT; the average inductor current is controlled meanwhile so the output reaches its set value.
Above 163 °C junction temperature both FETs stop switching. When the die cools below 141 °C, the device starts again through soft start.

The device is shut down when VEN is below 0.95 V, and the converter is off while VIN is under its 3.58 V UVLO falling threshold. With both EN and VIN above their thresholds it is active, in one of four conditions by load: CCM at fixed frequency when the load exceeds half the inductor ripple (all versions); DCM at fixed frequency below that (PFM versions); PFM with falling frequency at very light load (PFM versions); or FPWM at fixed frequency down to no load (FPWM versions). CCM gives the least ripple and the full 3 A.

Below half the CCM ripple current the converter runs discontinuously, turning the low-side switch off when the inductor current falls to IZC, 20 mA typ. At lighter load, once the minimum on time or the minimum peak current IPEAK_MIN (0.48 A typ) is reached, the loop lowers the switching frequency to hold regulation, cutting switching loss further.

The converter stays in PWM over the whole load range, even at no load, by letting the inductor current reverse. Light-load efficiency is given up for low ripple, tight regulation and a constant frequency.

A higher frequency allows smaller inductors and output capacitors and a smaller, cheaper design, but adds switching loss and heat; the minimum on time, with the input and output voltages, also caps it. The design example uses 500 kHz.

Inductance, saturation current and RMS current matter most. Ripple grows with input voltage, so the minimum inductance is worked out at the highest input. RMS and peak inductor currents can be high during an overcurrent event, and the saturation current must exceed the peak current limit. Lower inductance gives faster transients, lower DCR and smaller size, but too little raises ripple, can trip overcurrent at full load, adds core loss and output ripple; peak current mode control needs enough ripple for a clean comparator signal.

COUT sets steady-state ripple, loop stability and the overshoot and undershoot on load steps. Ripple has an ESR part and a capacitive part. On a large load step the output capacitors carry the difference for the eight or more cycles the loop needs to bring the inductor current to the new level, which usually sets the minimum capacitance when regulation must be tight.

A high-frequency ceramic decoupling capacitor of 4.7 µF or more, X5R or X7R, is recommended, rated above the maximum input; twice the maximum input is recommended to allow for ceramic derating. A further 0.1 µF right at the pins filters high frequencies. The design example uses two 4.7 µF, 50 V X7R parts with about 10 mΩ ESR and 1 A current rating.

The input supply, 4.5 V to 36 V, must be well regulated, able to supply the peak input current, and of low enough resistance that an input current step does not pull VIN into UVLO. When the supply is more than a few inches away, bulk capacitance beside the ceramics may be needed; a 10 µF or 22 µF electrolytic is typical.

Place CIN as close as possible to VIN and GND, and ground the input and output capacitors to local top-layer copper tied to GND; the input loop carries the high di/dt current and is the key to low EMI. Keep the SW trace to the inductor short and only as wide as the load current needs. Put the output capacitors near the inductor's output end with a short ground return to GND. Keep the FB net short with both divider resistors next to the FB pin; FB is high impedance and noise sensitive, while the trace from VOUT to the divider may be long. Where accuracy at the load matters, sense at the load and route the sense trace away from SW and the inductor, ideally on another layer with a ground plane between. Use a mid-layer ground plane for shielding and heat, make VIN, VOUT and ground wide, and give GND, VIN and SW large copper areas with an array of thermal vias to inner and bottom ground planes, keeping the junction below 125 °C.

The input bypass capacitor sits beside VIN and GND, the inductor and output capacitor beside SW, the boost capacitor and feedback resistors on the CB, EN and FB side, with a ground trace under the IC on the top layer, extra vias to the ground plane at the output capacitor, and a bottom-layer trace from the SW node to the boost capacitor.
